"During the third quarter, we achieved key milestones with both clinical programs: initiating dosing in our TEMPO-1 Phase 3 study of sutantatug envedotin in oropharyngeal cancer and announcing positive topline data from our CANYON-1 Phase 1b study of CRB-913 in obesity,” said Yuval Cohen, Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer of Corbus.

For CRB-913, our topline CANYON-1 data demonstrated, for the first time, that a highly peripherally restricted CB1 inverse agonist can deliver a safe and tolerable therapeutic alternative with competitive weight loss to oral GLP-1s.
• Reported topline data in the CANYON-1 Phase 1b trial, a 16-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study that enrolled 254 obese, non-diabetic adults at multiple U.S. sites.

No plateau was observed at any dose. o CRB-913 was associated with a favorable safety profile and notably fewer and milder gastrointestinal (GI) adverse events based on cross-trial comparison with published data of currently marketed oral GLP-1 drugs. o Taken together, these data support CRB-913’s potential to establish a new class of oral, non-incretin obesity medicines. o Topline data press release available here (link: https://ir.corbuspharma.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/478/corbus-pharmaceuticals-announces-positive-topline-data-from-canyon-1-study-of-daily-oral-crb-913-for-the-treatment-of-obesity).

There can be no assurance that TEMPO-1 will achieve its primary or secondary endpoints, that sutantatug envedotin will receive accelerated or full approval from the FDA, that previously reported clinical data, including topline data from CANYON-1, will be replicated in later-stage or larger controlled studies, that results of cross-trial comparisons will be confirmed, or that the Company will be able to obtain additional capital on acceptable terms or at all.
